critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope is mentioned anywhere. This is a 3.2 M96 at 90.7k mi, where bore scoring is a known risk.

The listing and Carfax show no IMS retrofit and no engine number. A 2005 engine likely carries the single-row bearing, the highest-failure variant. Bearing type remains unconfirmed until the engine number or an invoice is seen.
There is no filter inspection record. Recent oil changes appear (Carfax 07/20/2026) but nothing on the filter media.
There is no fault memory, cam deviation or overrev printout. 'Inspection / Service' (07/2025) has no details.
The last documented top check was 04/2009 at the dealer, per Carfax. The hardtop is fitted in all the attached photos, so the soft top is not examined here. There is no drain or footwell evidence.

The coolant flush (08/2026) is a listing claim only, with no Carfax entry. Carfax shows a radiator fan motor replaced 05/2018, which is not radiator or condenser work. There is no reported entry for a water pump, thermostat or expansion tank in 21 years.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: the VIN, a clean-title Carfax with 47 records, a coherent mileage trail and disclosed flaws. The maintenance half is partial. Carfax corroborates oil changes and engine mounts, but the AOS, coolant and brake fluid work are listing claims without invoices. There is no IMS, borescope or water pump evidence. There is also a roughly 28k-mile stretch (09/2019-10/2024) with no reported service entries.

condition.rationale: Photos show tidy paint and a clean frunk, with disclosed minor chips and moderate seat creasing. The 2020 damage event has no repair detail. Nothing mechanical is stated as wrong, but engine internals (IMS, bores), cooling and suspension are unproven at 90.7k mi.

price_value.rationale: $23,000 sits above the top of the $16,403-$21,696 fair-value band (mid $20,986). That is before allowing for an unaddressed single-row IMS exposure on a 2005, five owners and an undocumented damage event.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual 987 S fits the keeper category. However, a 2005 M96 without an IMS retrofit or borescope is the riskiest 987 provenance for a long-term car, and the above-market price works against cash preservation in bridge mode.

logistics.rationale: Tucson is about 850 miles away, a moderate fly-and-drive trip. Porsche-capable independent shops that know the car exist locally, but the seller's agreement to a PPI is not stated. AZ emissions history suggests CA smog is feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It has several desirable traits: a 6-speed manual, Dark Olive Metallic, Sand Beige full leather, Sport Chrono Plus (the dash clock is visible) and an OEM hardtop. These are tempered by gold aftermarket wheels, gold-painted vents and a CarPlay unit replacing the PCM, though the original PCM is included.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for scoring, especially the bank 2 cylinders, and check cold-start rattle.
Determine IMS bearing type from the engine number, and check for an RMS or IMS-flange weep at the bellhousing.
Cut the oil filter for metallic debris, and get a Durametric/PIWIS readout of cam deviations, fault memory and overrev ranges.
Inspect the 2020 damage area with a paint-depth gauge, panel gaps and repair quality.
Check the water pump for weep or play, look for coolant crust on the expansion tank and lines, and inspect the front radiators and condensers for debris and corrosion behind the gold-painted grilles.
Remove the hardtop and cycle the soft top. Inspect the cables, rams, rear window seam, drains and footwell or under-seat moisture.
Assess the clutch and dual-mass flywheel (judder, slip, engagement point), and check the short shifter installation and linkage.
Check front control arms, coffin-arm bushings, top mounts and tie rods at 90.7k mi, plus ride height.
Verify wheel and tire sizes, staggered fitment and DOT dates.
Check the AOS for startup smoke or a vacuum fault, and confirm the claimed AOS replacement is visible.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean borescope and filter cut plus an IMS retrofit invoice tied to this engine number.
Up: invoices for the AOS, coolant work and the 2020 damage repair, plus a price closer to the fair-value mid-point.
Down: scoring on the borescope, metal in the filter, or out-of-spec cam deviations.
Down: evidence of panel repaint or structural repair beyond the claimed cosmetic damage, or the seller declining a PPI.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, well-optioned 987 S belongs in the keeper category. As a 2005 M96 with no IMS or bore evidence, priced above comps, it is an engine-risk keeper that works against the current cash-preservation, accelerated-bridge plan.
evidence.rationale: The listing and Carfax together establish a clean-title, 5-owner, 2005 Boxster S 6-speed with a consistent mileage trail (90,580 at 07/2026) and a FL-then-AZ history. Carfax corroborates the early Porsche-dealer service and the recent engine mount and oil work. Observed issues are a 03/24/2020 damage event with no repair documentation, about 28,000 miles under owner 4 with no reported service entries, disclosed paint chips, and wheels that appear to differ between views. The asking price of $23,000 sits above the $16,403-$21,696 fair-value band. Several of the most relevant maintenance claims (AOS, coolant flush, brake fluid) have no invoice and no Carfax entry. The decisive 987.1 items remain open: IMS bearing type on a 2005 engine, bore condition, cooling-system components, the clutch, and the soft top. The specification itself (rare color, Sport Chrono Plus, hardtop, manual) is a genuine strength, offset by reversible cosmetic modifications.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the engine number, the AOS, coolant and 2020 damage invoices, and written agreement to a PPI with borescope and filter cut at a Tucson Porsche specialist before any deposit.
